record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Give a rigorous meaning to the Wulff construction for such interface models.

evidence.quote: An other important problem is to give rigorous meaning to the Wulff construction for such models [DM].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a gradient interface model on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (with $d \geq 2$), in which a random height field $\varphi : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ describes a $(d+1)$-dimensional interface separating two coexisting phases. For a finite domain $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ with prescribed boundary condition $\psi$ on $\partial \Lambda$, the Gibbs measure is
$$\mu_\Lambda^\psi(d\varphi) = \frac{1}{Z_\Lambda^\psi} \exp\!\left(-\sum_{\{x,y\} \subset \Lambda \cup \partial\Lambda,\ |x-y|=1} V(\varphi(x) - \varphi(y))\right) \prod_{x \in \Lambda} d\varphi(x),$$
where $V : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a (symmetric, strictly convex, sufficiently regular) interaction potential and $\varphi(x) = \psi(x)$ for $x \in \partial \Lambda$. Assume that the model admits a well-defined surface tension $\sigma : \mathbb{R}^d \to [0,\infty)$ associated with tilted boundary conditions (so that for $u \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\sigma(u)$ is the rate of decay of the partition function under a tilt $\psi_u(x) = u \cdot x$).

The Wulff functional assigns to each sufficiently regular bounded region $W \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ the surface energy
$$\mathcal{W}(W) = \int_{\partial W} \sigma(\nu_W(s))\, dS(s),$$
where $\nu_W$ is the outward unit normal. The Wulff shape is the minimizer (up to translation and dilation) of $\mathcal{W}$ subject to a volume constraint.

Formulate and prove, in a mathematically rigorous fashion, the Wulff construction for this class of interface models. Specifically: given a conditioning that forces the interface to enclose an atypical volume (or equivalently, conditioning on a large value of $\sum_x \varphi(x)$ or on a phase-separation event), show that in the thermodynamic limit and after appropriate rescaling, the typical macroscopic shape of the interface concentrates on the minimizer of the Wulff functional $\mathcal{W}$ under the corresponding volume constraint, with explicit large-deviation rate given by the surface tension $\sigma$.
artifact.category_tag: Wulff construction for gradient interface models
artifact.status_search_result: For the 2D Ising model, independent percolation, and the random-cluster model in two dimensions, the Wulff construction has been rigorously established (Dobrushin–Kotecký–Shlosman, Pfister, Ioffe–Schonmann, Bodineau, Cerf–Pisztora, etc.), and in higher dimensions for Ising at low temperature (Cerf–Pisztora, Bodineau). For continuous-height gradient ∇φ interface models with strictly convex potentials, surface tension and large-deviation principles have been developed (Funaki–Spohn, Deuschel–Giacomin–Ioffe), but a fully general rigorous Wulff construction in this setting is not established in the literature reviewed; the precise status depends on the specific class of interface models, and we could not verify a complete resolution.

status_evidence.title: Wulff Construction: A Global Shape from Local Interaction
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph by Dobrushin–Kotecký–Shlosman proving the Wulff construction rigorously for the 2D Ising model at low temperatures.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous Wulff construction is known for 2D Ising at low temperature.

status_evidence.title: The Wulff construction in statistical mechanics and combinatorics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing rigorous Wulff results for Ising, percolation, and random-cluster models in two dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: In dimension two, Wulff construction is established for Ising, percolation, and random-cluster models.

status_evidence.title: A microscopic justification of the Wulff construction
status_evidence.snippet: Dobrushin–Kotecký–Shlosman provided the first microscopic justification of the Wulff construction.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous microscopic justification exists in specific lattice models, not in full generality for all interface models.
